basis: Cutaneous and gastrointestinal venous malformations define disease; HPO coagulation dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Bone pain alone does not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: HPO coagulation abnormalities in 30-79% support impaired coagulation; bleeding alone would not suffice.

basis: Ferritin iron-storage defect; alopecia 10/11 and seizures 1/2 support involvement. Neurologic frequency is uncertain because of the small sample; normal blood counts exclude a blood-cell disorder.

decisions.neurologic: involved: seizures in 1/2 assessed patients meet the supplied frequency threshold; small sample and variable dominant/recessive expression reduce confidence.

basis: Enterocyte microvillus atrophy; sustained bicarbonate loss causes acidosis (2/2). Bronchiectasis 1/1 lacks established direct attribution; osteopenia may be nutritional or treatment-related.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis is recorded in 1/1, but intrinsic airway damage from this enterocyte disorder is unestablished; frequency alone does not establish direct causation.

basis: Defining cerebral arteriopathy and hypogonadism; cerebral ischemic/hemorrhagic injury is frequent, with stroke-like episodes 5/7; cataracts 4/7. Hair graying alone is insufficient.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral injury follows the defining arteriopathy; stroke-like episodes occur in 5/7, with ischemic stroke and hemorrhage frequent. The defining lesion is vascular.

basis: Reported short broad great toes and intellectual disability define this sparsely documented syndrome. [Description](https://checkorphan.org/disease/collins-sakati-syndrome/)

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: short, broad great toes are reported as a defining skeletal malformation; evidence is sparse.

basis: Immune dysregulation with lymphopenia and autoimmune cytopenias; inflammatory dermatitis 30-79%. Direct intestinal lesions and bronchiectasis are annotated at 5-29%; diarrhea alone is insufficient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea occurs in 30-79%, but documented colorectal infiltration, colitis and atrophic gastritis are each 5-29%; common direct intestinal damage is not established by these HPO data.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: atopic dermatitis is annotated in 30-79%; persistent inflammatory skin disease in this immune dysregulation syndrome qualifies beyond a transient rash.

basis: EBV-driven B-cell proliferation with lung disease; CNS 40%, skin 34% in the NCI series. Skin omitted at cap, prioritizing CNS severity. [NCI](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7162687/)

decisions.haematologic: primary: a clonal B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder is a blood-cell disease even when its lesions occupy extranodal organs.
decisions.neurologic: involved: direct CNS occupation occurs in about 40% in the NCI series; retained for frequency and severity under the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: none (cap): destructive cutaneous infiltration occurs in about 34%; CNS involvement is more frequent (~40%) and more severe, so it takes the final available axis.

basis: Bile-acid synthesis defect causes cholestatic liver disease and digestive failure; malabsorption 80-99%. Coagulopathy 30-79% and rickets 5/13 can follow separate vitamin deficiencies.

decisions.haematologic: none: coagulopathy (30-79%) commonly follows vitamin K malabsorption, rather than direct coagulation injury. [Case](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13256-026-06698-1)

basis: Infection-associated periodontal inflammation directly destroys dental attachment and alveolar jaw bone; rapid alveolar bone loss is a defining diagnostic feature.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the definition explicitly requires destructive alveolar bone loss; jaw bone is skeletal tissue, and defining bone destruction qualifies regardless of its dental location.

basis: Peroxisomal disorder with defining developmental impairment (20/20); retinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss usually >30%. Common hepatic disease omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none (cap): hepatic fibrosis/dysfunction is common (>30%), but neurologic impairment and the characteristic disabling retinal and hearing degeneration take priority.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment in 20/20 and the NALD/IRD neurodevelopmental phenotype define this peroxisomal syndrome.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss is a characteristic common manifestation (>30%). [GTR](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/conditions/C0282527/)
